record.original_question: For shape spaces of closed hypersurfaces bounding the same volume, equipped with hydrodynamically induced nonlocal H^{-1/2} metrics arising from dynamic boundaries or vortex sheets, can one describe their differential geometry?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth closed oriented manifold of dimension $n-1$, and consider the space
$$\mathrm{Imm}_{\mathrm{vol}}(M, \mathbb{R}^n) = \{ q : M \hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}^n \text{ smooth immersion bounding a fixed enclosed volume } V_0 \},$$
together with its quotient
$$\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{vol}}(M, \mathbb{R}^n) = \mathrm{Imm}_{\mathrm{vol}}(M, \mathbb{R}^n) / \mathrm{Diff}(M),$$
the shape space of unparametrized closed hypersurfaces of $\mathbb{R}^n$ enclosing a region of fixed volume $V_0$. Tangent vectors at a shape $\Sigma = q(M)$ may be identified with normal vector fields $h \, \nu$ on $\Sigma$ satisfying $\int_\Sigma h \, \mathrm{dvol}_\Sigma = 0$, where $\nu$ is the outward unit normal.

For each such $\Sigma$, equip the tangent space with the nonlocal Riemannian metric
$$G_\Sigma(h_1 \nu, h_2 \nu) = \int_\Sigma h_1 \, ((-\Delta_\Sigma)^{-1/2} h_2)\, \mathrm{dvol}_\Sigma,$$
where $\Delta_\Sigma$ denotes the Laplace–Beltrami operator on $\Sigma$ (acting on functions of mean zero, where it is invertible). Equivalently, $G_\Sigma$ is the $H^{-1/2}(\Sigma)$ inner product on normal speeds, and it is the metric induced on shape space by the hydrodynamic problem of an incompressible irrotational fluid filling the bounded region with a free (dynamic) boundary, or by the vortex-sheet formulation in which the velocity is reconstructed from a sheet strength on $\Sigma$.

Describe the differential geometry of the infinite-dimensional Riemannian manifold $(\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{vol}}(M, \mathbb{R}^n), G)$. In particular:

(a) Determine the Levi-Civita connection of $G$ and write explicit formulas for it.

(b) Compute the Riemannian (sectional) curvature of $G$.

(c) Identify the geodesic equation on $\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{vol}}(M, \mathbb{R}^n)$ and relate it to the equations of motion of a free-boundary incompressible irrotational fluid and to vortex-sheet dynamics.

(d) Investigate basic global properties such as geodesic completeness/incompleteness, non-vanishing of the geodesic distance, and existence of conjugate points.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on shape-space Riemannian geometry (Bauer–Harms–Michor and collaborators) treats local Sobolev metrics $H^s$ for integer or positive $s$, almost-local and curvature-weighted metrics, but the differential geometry (connection, curvature, geodesic completeness) of the nonlocal $H^{-1/2}$ metric induced by free-boundary fluid flow or vortex sheets on volume-preserving hypersurfaces has not, to our knowledge, been described in published work. No source verifying a solution was located, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Curvature weighted metrics on shape space of hypersurfaces in n-space
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Sobolev and almost-local metrics on shape spaces of hypersurfaces; does not treat the nonlocal H^{-1/2} hydrodynamic metric.
status_evidence.claim: Existing shape-space geometry literature focuses on different metric families.
